title: Normalized realization interfaces for integral quotient systems
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site use the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the quotient system calculus [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. For whole-system inverse image and scalar change [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], define the constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction and its counit in the derived category of whole towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], normalized on K-injective tower resolutions by the ordinary limit cone. Define a Roos realization model by its natural comparison with total derived limit and its limit-tuple/zero-shifted-coordinate normalization. Define pullback and scalar realization models for the recorded completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] by natural realization isomorphisms. Scalar realization is normalized on every flat-term K-flat representative and every whole-system adjunction-coherent simultaneous quotient presentation: its reduction isomorphism transposes under the reduction/total-limit and constant-tower/total-limit adjunctions to the localization of the strict tensor-unit map determined by the finite identifications. This is the same coherence condition used for pullback realization. Pullback realization is normalized on every flat-term K-flat representative and every whole-system coherent simultaneous quotient presentation: transposing its derived comparison under reduction/total-limit and then under constant-tower/total-limit equals the localization of the strict tensor-unit map specified by its finite identifications. This fixes the entire derived comparison, not merely its finite evaluations. The normalization uses the actual quotient transitions, pullback unit and tensor generators, and the universal change-of-rings counit [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

proof.text: Construct the constant-tower adjunction using the exact-functor/total-right-derived adjunction. On a K-injective tower, Adjunction.derivedε_fac_app gives its counit after precomposition by the derived unit. Cancel that unit and transport along quotientCompQhIso and mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh to obtain the ordinary limit-cone formula.

Identify module sheaves over the horizontal-constant completed coefficient sheaf on the sequence site with strict towers of completed-coefficient modules. Construct the equivalence by restricting to vertical slices and assembling their horizontal maps; its unit and counit are identity maps on sections. The completed coefficient projections form a natural transformation by the ordinary limit cone equations, giving the ring map to the quotient sequence sheaf. Restriction along this map followed by the equivalence is coefficientSequenceRestriction: its component objects and section maps satisfy the existing unique characterization. The public sheafRingDerivedCoefficientAdjunction theorem applied to the existing derived-change-of-rings witness makes exact derived restriction a right adjoint. Compose this right adjoint with the derived equivalence and transport it along mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso to the specified whole-system derived restriction.

Apply Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit to the reduction adjunction and the composite constant-tower/system-extension adjunction. Its inverse comparison is leftAdjointUniq in the opposite order. Adjunction.comp_counit_app then gives the displayed reduction-counit formula.

For a tower complex, form the product of its ordinary limit projections. The limit cone equations show its composite with 1 minus shift is zero. Mathlib mappingCocone.lift with zero degree-minus-one cochain constructs the required map. Product extensionality fixes its first coordinate; the zero second coordinate and mappingCocone.id_X fix each degree of the whole map, proving uniqueness.

The object component of coefficientSequenceRestriction_exists identifies the restricted evaluation with scalarReductionRestriction of evaluation. Scalar restriction preserves the underlying abelian sheaf, so coefficientSequenceEvaluationAb_eq gives the equality of section types.

Require the pullback presentation comparison to transpose, under the two entire-system adjunctions, to the localization of its strict tensor-unit map. The finite section formula fixes this strict map, and injectivity of both Hom bijections fixes the derived comparison. Canonical ordinary quotient presentations with the derived adjunction comparison satisfy this condition by the derived Hom formula. This removes the invisible-twist obstruction without imposing any boundedness or condition on the input complex.

Specify the scalar representative normalization on the same whole-system adjunction-coherent presentations already used for pullback. This reuses IsIntegralComparisonPresentationCoherent verbatim: it fixes the double transpose of e by the strict tensor-unit map, so its meaning is an equality in the entire tower derived category. No data construction or existence assertion is added by this definition.

For a tower complex, form the product of its ordinary limit projections. The limit cone equations show its composite with 1 minus shift is zero. Mathlib mappingCocone.lift with zero degree-minus-one cochain constructs the required map. Product extensionality fixes its first coordinate; the zero second coordinate and mappingCocone.id_X fix each degree of the whole map, proving uniqueness.

The object component of coefficientSequenceRestriction_exists identifies the restricted evaluation with scalarReductionRestriction of evaluation. Scalar restriction preserves the underlying abelian sheaf, so coefficientSequenceEvaluationAb_eq gives the equality of section types.

Require the pullback presentation comparison to transpose, under the two entire-system adjunctions, to the localization of its strict tensor-unit map. The finite section formula fixes this strict map, and injectivity of both Hom bijections fixes the derived comparison. Canonical ordinary quotient presentations with the derived adjunction comparison satisfy this condition by the derived Hom formula. This removes the invisible-twist obstruction without imposing any boundedness or condition on the input complex.

previous.old_statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site use the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the quotient system calculus [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. For whole-system inverse image and scalar change [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], define the constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction and its counit in the derived category of whole towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], normalized on K-injective tower resolutions by the ordinary limit cone. Define a Roos realization model by its natural comparison with total derived limit and its limit-tuple/zero-shifted-coordinate normalization. Define pullback and scalar realization models for the recorded completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] by natural realization isomorphisms normalized on every flat-term K-flat representative and every simultaneous quotient presentation. The normalization uses the actual quotient transitions, pullback unit and tensor generators, and the universal change-of-rings counit [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].
previous.what: Repair the false universal pullback normalization: a presentation was constrained only by its finite derived evaluations and strict quotient transitions, so it admitted twists of e invisible at every finite derived evaluation. The generator comparison q is fixed by kappa, but a whole derived limit sees such a twist. Add the missing whole-system adjunction coherence condition. The new condition fixes e before taking the limit and is satisfied by the ordinary tensor-derived presentation. The underlying rings, complexes, derived functors, natural realization and generator formulas are unchanged. This is an explicit correction of an auxiliary interface, not a proof of the previous false version. The pre-existing scalar and completion versions have the analogous issue and are outside this item.

old_proof.text: Construct the constant-tower adjunction using the exact-functor/total-right-derived adjunction. On a K-injective tower, Adjunction.derivedε_fac_app gives its counit after precomposition by the derived unit. Cancel that unit and transport along quotientCompQhIso and mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh to obtain the ordinary limit-cone formula.

Identify module sheaves over the horizontal-constant completed coefficient sheaf on the sequence site with strict towers of completed-coefficient modules. Construct the equivalence by restricting to vertical slices and assembling their horizontal maps; its unit and counit are identity maps on sections. The completed coefficient projections form a natural transformation by the ordinary limit cone equations, giving the ring map to the quotient sequence sheaf. Restriction along this map followed by the equivalence is coefficientSequenceRestriction: its component objects and section maps satisfy the existing unique characterization. The public sheafRingDerivedCoefficientAdjunction theorem applied to the existing derived-change-of-rings witness makes exact derived restriction a right adjoint. Compose this right adjoint with the derived equivalence and transport it along mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso to the specified whole-system derived restriction.
